question: How is a duplicate invoice detected?
gold: Same supplier GSTIN and normalised invoice number (spaces, slashes, hyphens, leading zeros and /A, /R or -REV suffixes removed), or same supplier, invoice date and total within ₹1.
answer_text:
Status: answered
Answer: A duplicate invoice is detected by comparing each invoice, before indexing, against invoices received in the last 18 months for the same supplier. [1] The comparison uses a normalised invoice number: remove spaces, slashes, hyphens and leading zeros, and drop a trailing suffix of /A, /R or -REV. [1] Two invoices are a suspected duplicate when the supplier GSTIN and normalised number match, or when the supplier, invoice date and total amount (within ₹1) match. [1] Suspected duplicates go to the exception queue as DUP_SUSPECT and are never posted until a Senior Processor clears them. [1] The duplicate check is run with the button at the top of the screen, and if the system shows an amber flag you stop and raise DUP_SUSPECT without overriding. [2] In practice, the duplicate check is the first thing done before anything else, and if it flags amber you stop. [3]
Expert tip: Duplicate invoices must be sent to DUP_SUSPECT with a note and not overridden.
